mainTopic: Pieces of an אשרה and a nest on it; found vessels with figures of the sun, moon and dragon, and רב ששת's list of forbidden images
overview: The גמרא asks why fallen leaves of a worshipped tree stay forbidden, since shavings cut from an idol are permitted. רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע answers that an idol does not lose its status through its natural growth. ריש לקיש then challenges רבי יוחנן from a משנה that lets a person knock down a nest from an אשרה. The גמרא defends רבי יוחנן in two ways: either the bird brought the branches from elsewhere, or the permission covers only the chicks, not the nest. Chicks are permitted and eggs are forbidden, and רב אשי adds that chicks still needing their mother count as eggs. A new משנה rules that found vessels with figures of the sun, moon or a dragon must be thrown into ים המלח. אביי explains that people worship many things, but they only make images of these three in order to worship them. The גמרא then asks whether רב ששת's list of forbidden images is about making them or finding them, and tests each clause, with the discussion continuing on the next amud.

steps.title: Why are fallen leaves forbidden if shavings are permitted?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the rule that fallen leaves of an אשרה are forbidden. It compares them to shavings cut from an idol, which are permitted even though the idol itself still stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: But look at shavings: the main idol is still there, and yet it was taught that if a gentile shaved it for its own sake, the idol is forbidden but its shavings are permitted!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is attacking the earlier ruling that leaves which fall off a worshipped tree stay forbidden. It points to the case of שיפויין, shavings, as a contradiction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With shavings, the idol is still standing, yet the pieces that came off are permitted. Leaves that fall off an אשרה should be the same: the tree is still standing and the leaves have separated from it. So why should the leaves be forbidden?

keyTerms.meaning: Shavings or scrapings taken off an object
For its own sake (for the idol's benefit)

phrases.english: But look at shavings,
where the main idol still exists,
and it teaches: if done for its sake, it is forbidden,
phrases.notes: "For its sake" means the gentile shaved the idol to fix it up for worship, not to ruin it.

phrases.english: but its shavings are permitted!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling just discussed before this section, that fallen leaves of an אשרה remain forbidden.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that leaves which fall from an אשרה stay forbidden
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Shavings separated from an idol that is still standing are permitted. Leaves separated from a tree that is still standing should be permitted for the same reason.

steps.title: An idol does not lose its status through natural growth
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע explains that leaves are different. Their falling is part of the tree's natural life cycle, and that kind of process cannot cancel the status of עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע said: because an idol does not become nullified through the way it naturally grows.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Leaves falling off a tree is something natural, so it does not remove their forbidden status.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Shavings come off because someone actively cut them. Leaves fall because that is what trees naturally do. Something that happens as part of the tree's normal growth cannot count as the idol being cancelled.

keyTerms.meaning: Becomes nullified or loses its status

phrases.aramaic: רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אָמַר:
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua said:
Because an idol is not nullified
through its natural manner of growth.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from shavings.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the two cases: separation through natural growth versus separation done actively
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any piece that separates from a standing idol should be permitted, like shavings.
steps.terutzMaskana: Pieces that separate through the tree's natural growth process, like falling leaves, keep their forbidden status.
steps.whatToRemember: Falling leaves are part of the tree's natural growth, so they do not cancel the status of עבודה זרה.

steps.title: ריש לקיש cites the case of a nest on top of a tree
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן לקיש brings a source to challenge רבי יוחנן. It deals with a bird's nest at the top of a הקדש tree and a nest at the top of an אשרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן לקיש challenged רבי יוחנן: a nest at the top of a tree belonging to הקדש may not be used, but there is no מעילה for using it. A nest at the top of an אשרה may be knocked down with a pole.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings back the main argument: רבי יוחנן holds that an idol that breaks by itself stays forbidden. ריש לקיש quotes a source to set up his challenge, and the next step explains how it works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source rules that a nest on an אשרה can be knocked down with a pole and then used. Here ריש לקיש is only presenting the source; how it challenges רבי יוחנן becomes clear in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Property belonging to the בית המקדש
A tree that is worshipped as an idol
Knock it down with a pole

phrases.aramaic: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish objected to Rabbi Yochanan:
phrases.notes: The source he quotes is a משנה in מעילה.

phrases.english: A nest at the top of a tree of the Temple property —
one may not benefit from it, but there is no liability for misuse,
one at the top of an ashera —
he may knock it down with a pole.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side question about leaves and goes back to the main argument between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's view that an idol that breaks by itself remains forbidden
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה permits a nest on an אשרה. The next step shows why this is a problem for רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: The assumption: the bird built the nest from the tree's own branches
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the challenge. If the bird broke branches off the אשרה and built its nest from them, those pieces broke off with no person involved. Yet the nest is permitted, which supports ריש לקיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: You would assume this is a case where the bird broke branches off the tree and built its nest with them, and yet it teaches that he may knock it down with a pole.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the assumption that turns the משנה into a challenge against רבי יוחנן. Watch for the next step to question this assumption.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Branches broken off by a bird are like an idol that broke by itself, since no person did it. If the nest made from them is permitted, it seems that an idol which breaks by itself loses its status. That is ריש לקיש's view and goes against רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: It enters your mind / you would have assumed
And it (the bird) built a nest

steps.confusionAlert: The words קא סלקא דעתך signal only a first assumption. In the next step the גמרא reads the case differently.

phrases.english: It enters your mind,
that it is a case where it broke branches from it
and built a nest with them,
phrases.notes: "It" is the bird, and "them" are the branches from the אשרה itself.

phrases.english: and it teaches: he may knock it down with a pole.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes ריש לקיש's challenge by explaining the case the משנה is assumed to describe.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling that an idol broken without human action stays forbidden
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The branches broke off through the bird, with no human involved, and the משנה still permits the nest. So an idol that breaks without a person seems to lose its status.
steps.whyThisMatters: The whole challenge depends on where the nest's branches came from. That is exactly the point the גמרא examines in the next step.

steps.title: The bird brought branches from somewhere else
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the challenge to רבי יוחנן. The case of the nest is one where the bird brought branches from elsewhere, not from the אשרה itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? A case where the bird brought branches from elsewhere and built its nest with them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי יוחנן by explaining that the nest was built from outside branches, so it was never part of the אשרה at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש's challenge only works if the nest came from pieces of the אשרה that broke off on their own. If the branches came from other trees, they never had the status of עבודה זרה. So the nest being permitted proves nothing against רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: "What case are we dealing with here?" The גמרא is about to narrow the case to a specific situation.
From elsewhere, from the outside world

phrases.english: What case are we dealing with here?
For example, where it brought branches from elsewhere,
phrases.notes: "It" is the bird. The branches came from other trees, not from the אשרה.

phrases.english: and built its nest with them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 4 by defining the case differently.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא): the nest is made of outside material.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The bird broke branches off the אשרה itself, so pieces that broke off on their own would be permitted.
steps.terutzMaskana: The branches came from elsewhere, so the nest was never עבודה זרה, and רבי יוחנן's rule stands.

steps.title: The wording about the הקדש nest supports this reading
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings support from the same source. For a הקדש tree it says one may not benefit from the nest, but there is no מעילה. That fits well if the branches came from elsewhere.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wording is also exact this way. About הקדש it teaches: one may not benefit, but there is no מעילה. If you say the bird brought branches from elsewhere, that explains it: no benefit is a rabbinic rule, and no מעילה under Torah law, because the branches are not holy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the wording of the source fits the answer from Step 5. This sets up the contrast that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "Not benefit, but no מעילה" means the nest is only forbidden מדרבנן. That makes sense if the branches were never part of the הקדש tree, since outside branches are not truly holy. The same reading then carries over to the אשרה nest.

keyTerms.meaning: "It is also exact": the wording itself supports this explanation
Property given to the בית המקדש
Liable for מְעִילָה, the Torah prohibition of using הקדש for personal benefit

phrases.english: The wording is also exact this way,
for it teaches about הקדש:
one may not benefit, but one is not liable for מעילה;

phrases.aramaic: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא דְּאַיְיתַי עֵצִים מֵעָלְמָא,
phrases.english: granted, if you say it brought branches from elsewhere,
that explains why it teaches about הקדש:
one may not benefit, but there is no מעילה:
no benefit by rabbinic law,
and no מעילה by Torah law,
since the branches are not holy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings textual support for the answer in Step 5.
steps.raayaObject: The answer that the bird brought branches from elsewhere.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ruling for the הקדש tree: no benefit, but no מעילה.

steps.title: Branches from the tree itself would be holy
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes the support by showing the other reading fails. If the bird broke branches off the הקדש tree, those branches are holy, so there should be מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if you say the bird broke branches off the tree and built its nest with them, why is there no מעילה? Those branches are holy!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא completes its support by showing the other way of reading the case does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Branches taken from a הקדש tree carry its holiness, so using them should bring מעילה. Since the source says there is no מעילה, the branches must have come from elsewhere. This backs up Step 5 and helps רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: They are holy (they have the status of הקדש)

phrases.english: But if you say
that it broke branches off the tree itself,
and built its nest with them,
why is there no מעילה?
Those branches are holy!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ שֶׁשִּׁבְּרָה עֵצִים מִמֶּנּוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The second half of the support begun in Step 6. It rules out the other reading.
steps.raayaObject: That the nest was built from outside branches.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Branches from the הקדש tree itself would be holy and bring מעילה, which the source denies.

steps.title: The support fails: the branches may be new growths
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the support. The branches might have come from the tree itself, as growths that came after it became הקדש, and this תנא holds there is no מעילה on growths.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that a proof? We could be dealing with growths that came later, and this תנא holds there is no מעילה on growths.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the support from Steps 6 and 7 and shows the wording does not prove the branches came from elsewhere.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is another way to explain "no מעילה": the branches grew on the tree after it was given to הקדש. If this תנא holds that later growths do not bring מעילה, the branches could come from the tree itself. So the wording is no proof. The answer in Step 5 is still possible, but it is no longer forced.

keyTerms.meaning: "Is that a proof?" It rejects an argument as not compelling.
Growths: new parts that grew after the tree became הקדש
He holds (this is the תנא's view)

steps.confusionAlert: This step does not say the bird broke branches off the אשרה, and it does not cancel the answer in Step 5. It only shows that the הקדש wording is not a proof for that answer.
steps.whyThisMatters: It brings in a separate idea: some hold that new growths on a הקדש tree do not carry full holiness for מעילה.

phrases.english: Is that a proof?

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא בְּגִידּוּלִין הַבָּאִין לְאַחַר מִכָּאן עָסְקִינַן,
phrases.english: Here we are dealing with growths that came afterward,
phrases.notes: He means branches that grew on the tree after it was given to הקדש.

phrases.english: and this תנא holds there is no מעילה on growths.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the support brought in Steps 6 and 7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the wording. The answer in Step 5 is still possible.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: "No מעילה" can also be explained by later growths from the tree itself, so it does not prove the branches came from elsewhere.

steps.title: Another reading for רבי יוחנן: knock off the chicks
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו, quoting רבי יוחנן, says that 'יתיז' in the משנה means knocking off the chicks, not using the nest itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו says in the name of רבי יוחנן: What does 'he may knock off' mean? He may knock off the chicks.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second way to read the משנה so that it fits רבי יוחנן. The permission is only for the chicks, not the nest.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 5-8 tried to explain the משנה by saying the nest was built from outside branches, and the support for that was pushed off. Here רבי אבהו removes the problem another way. If the משנה only allows the chicks, it never permitted a nest made from pieces that broke off by themselves. So it is no challenge to רבי יוחנן at all.

keyTerms.meaning: He may knock off (with a stick)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Abbahu says that Rabbi Yochanan says:
What does "he may knock off" mean?
He may knock off the chicks.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: מַאי ״יַתִּיז״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the support in steps 6-7 was rejected in step 8, this gives a different way to defend רבי יוחנן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the wording of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to permit using the nest, even if it was made from pieces of the אשרה that broke off by themselves.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה only permits the chicks. The nest itself stays forbidden, so there is no proof for ריש לקיש.

steps.title: Chicks are permitted, eggs are forbidden, in both cases
steps.stepSummary: רבי יעקב explains to רבי ירמיה בר תחליפא that chicks are permitted and eggs are forbidden, both for a הקדש tree and for an אשרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יעקב said to רבי ירמיה בר תחליפא: I will explain it to you. Chicks, in both cases, are permitted. Eggs, in both cases, are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יעקב gives a clear rule for what is found in the nest. Chicks may be used and eggs may not, whether the tree is הקדש or an אשרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This builds on רבי אבהו's reading that the permission is about the chicks. Chicks can move around on their own, so they are not treated as part of the tree. Eggs just sit in the nest, so they are treated as connected to the forbidden tree.

keyTerms.meaning: I will explain it to you
Here and here, meaning in both cases

phrases.english: Rabbi Yaakov said
to Rabbi Yirmeya bar Tachlifa:
I will explain it to you:
With chicks, here and here they are permitted;
phrases.notes: "Here and here" means both the הקדש tree and the אשרה tree.

phrases.english: with eggs, here and here they are forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב לְרַבִּי יִרְמְיָה בַּר תַּחְלִיפָא: אַסְבְּרַהּ לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the full rule that comes from רבי אבהו's reading about the chicks.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Chicks in the nest are permitted and eggs are forbidden, for both a הקדש tree and an אשרה.

steps.title: Chicks that still need their mother count as eggs
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי adds that chicks that still depend on their mother are treated like eggs and are forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Chicks that still need their mother are like eggs.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי narrows the permission for chicks. Only chicks that can manage on their own are permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason chicks were permitted is that they are independent of the tree. A chick that still needs its mother is not yet independent. So it falls under the rule for eggs and is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: They are like, they are treated as

steps.whatToRemember: Final rule for the nest: grown chicks are permitted. Eggs, and chicks that still need their mother, are forbidden. This is true for both a הקדש tree and an אשרה.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
And chicks that still need their mother
are like eggs.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: וְאֶפְרוֹחִין שֶׁצְּרִיכִין לְאִמָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a limit to רבי יעקב's rule that chicks are permitted.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Chicks that still depend on their mother have the same status as eggs and are forbidden.

steps.title: New משנה: found vessels with figures of the sun, moon or dragon
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that someone who finds vessels with a figure of the sun, moon or a dragon must throw them into the Dead Sea. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says only respectable vessels are forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who finds vessels with a figure of the sun, a figure of the moon, or a figure of a dragon on them must take them to the Dead Sea. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: figures on respectable vessels are forbidden, and figures on disgraceful vessels are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches what to do with found vessels that have images often used in עבודה זרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא assumes such vessels were made for עבודה זרה, so no one may benefit from them. That is why they must be destroyed in the Dead Sea. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל makes it depend on how the vessel is used. A respectable vessel suggests the image is honored. A disgraceful vessel suggests it is not worshipped, so it is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: משנה, the start of a new משנה

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
One who finds vessels,
and upon them is a figure of the sun,
a figure of the moon, or a figure of a dragon —
he must take them to the Dead Sea.
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
those on respectable vessels are forbidden;
those on disgraceful vessels are permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הַמּוֹצֵא כֵּלִים וַעֲלֵיהֶם צוּרַת חַמָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The nest discussion is finished. A new משנה starts a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Found vessels with sun, moon or dragon figures must be destroyed. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל forbids them only on respectable vessels.

steps.title: Do people worship only these figures?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the משנה means that only the sun, moon and dragon are worshipped, and nothing else.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is this to say that only these are worshipped, and not anything else?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the short list in the משנה. This sets up the contradiction that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה names only three figures. That seems to suggest these are the only things people worship. The גמרא doubts that and is about to bring a source that shows otherwise.

keyTerms.meaning: גמרא, the start of the discussion on the משנה

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Is this to say that it is these that they worship,
but anything else they do not?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions what the משנה's list implies.
steps.kashyaTarget: The list of three figures in the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Listing only these figures implies that nothing else is worshipped, which seems unlikely.

steps.title: Contradiction: slaughtering for many things counts as idol offerings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a source showing that slaughtering for seas, rivers, the sun, an angel or even a small worm makes the animal an offering to idols, so people worship many things.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised a contradiction: One who slaughters for the sake of seas, rivers, the wilderness, the sun, the moon, the stars and constellations, מיכאל the great angel, or a small worm, these are offerings to the dead.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sharpens the question with a source that clashes with our משנה. This other source treats many different things as objects of worship.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If people worship even a small worm, then figures of many other things should also make a found vessel forbidden. So why does our משנה list only the sun, moon and dragon? The next step answers this.

keyTerms.meaning: And they raised a contradiction from another source
For the sake of, in honor of
Offerings to the dead, meaning sacrifices to idols

steps.confusionAlert: 'זבחי מתים' does not mean offerings for people who died. It is a name for sacrifices to עבודה זרה, which are forbidden.

phrases.english: And they raised a contradiction:
phrases.notes: The source quoted next is a משנה in חולין.

phrases.english: One who slaughters for the sake of seas,
for the sake of rivers, for the sake of the wilderness,
for the sake of the sun, for the sake of the moon,
for the sake of the stars and constellations,
for the sake of Michael the great minister,
phrases.notes: מיכאל is an angel, called the great minister.

phrases.english: for the sake of a small worm —
these are offerings to the dead!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source behind the question in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's limited list of figures
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another משנה treats slaughtering for many things, even a worm, as idol worship. So many kinds of figures should be forbidden, not just three.

steps.title: Worshipping what you find versus making images to worship
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that people worship anything they find, but they only make images of the three important things in order to worship them.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: When it comes to plain worship, people worship anything they come across. When it comes to making an image and then worshipping it, only these three important things are drawn and worshipped. Images of anything else are made just for decoration.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question from steps 13-14 about why the משנה lists only three images when people worship many things.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source in step 14 shows that people worship many real objects, like seas, rivers and even worms. The משנה is talking about images, not real objects. People only make images of the sun, moon and dragon in order to worship them, so an image of anything else is assumed to be decoration.

keyTerms.meaning: to fashion or draw an image

steps.confusionAlert: אביי does not say people only worship three things. They worship many things. They only make images of three things in order to worship them.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
As for worshipping, they worship anything they find;
as for fashioning an image and then worshipping it,
these three, which are important,
phrases.notes: The sun, moon and dragon from the משנה.

phrases.english: they draw them and worship them;
for anything else,
they make them merely for decoration.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: מִיפְלָח לְכֹל דְּמַשְׁכְּחִי פָּלְחִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in steps 13-14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between worshipping real objects and making images to worship
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to say that only three things are worshipped.
steps.terutzMaskana: Many things are worshipped, but only images of these three are made in order to worship them.

steps.title: רב ששת's combined list of forbidden images
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת gathers the strict rulings of the ברייתות: all images are permitted except the sun and moon, the human face, and the dragon.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת would collect the strict rulings of the ברייתות and teach: All constellations are permitted except the sun and moon. All faces are permitted except a human face. All figures are permitted except a dragon.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת gives one summary list of which images are forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He takes the strictest rule from each ברייתא and puts them together. His list adds the human face, which our משנה did not mention. The next steps will ask what case this list is about.

keyTerms.meaning: the strict rulings of the ברייתות

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet would gather
the stringencies of the baraitot and teach:
phrases.notes: He picks the strictest ruling from each of several ברייתות and joins them into one list.

phrases.english: All constellations are permitted,
except for the sun and the moon;
and all faces are permitted,
except for a human face;
and all figures are permitted,
except for the figure of a dragon.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְנַקֵּיט רַב שֵׁשֶׁת חוּמְרֵי מַתְנְיָיתָא וְתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new summary teaching on the same topic of forbidden images.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All images are permitted except the sun and moon, the human face, and the dragon.

steps.title: What case is רב ששת's list talking about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the first line of רב ששת's list and asks which case it refers to.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: All constellations are permitted except the sun and moon. What case are we dealing with here?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רב ששת's first rule and asks which case it is about. This sets up the next two steps, which try out possible answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "Permitted" could mean permitted to make such an image, or permitted to keep and use a found vessel that has such an image. The גמרא needs to know which one רב ששת means.

keyTerms.meaning: what case are we dealing with here?

phrases.english: The Master said:
All constellations are permitted,
except for the sun and the moon.
What are we dealing with here?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the first clause of רב ששת's list from step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether "permitted" refers to making the images or to finding vessels with the images.

steps.title: It cannot be about making images
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the idea that רב ששת is talking about making images, since the Torah forbids making images of any heavenly bodies.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is about someone who makes the images, are all constellations really permitted to make? Isn't it written, "You shall not make with Me"? This means you may not make the likeness of My attendants who serve before Me on high.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the first possible answer, that the list is about making images, and rejects it right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק "לא תעשון אתי" is explained to forbid making images of all heavenly bodies that serve ה׳, including the constellations. So רב ששת could not have said that making images of the constellations is permitted.

phrases.english: If we say it is about one who makes them,
if it is about one who makes them,
are all the constellations permitted?
But isn't it written: "You shall not make with Me"?
You shall not make the likeness of My attendants
who serve before Me on high.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵימָא בְּעוֹשֶׂה — אִי בְּעוֹשֶׂה, כׇּל הַמַּזָּלוֹת מִי שְׁרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests and rejects the first possible answer to step 17's question.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The reading that רב ששת's list is about making images.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The Torah forbids making images of all heavenly bodies, so all constellations cannot be permitted to make.

steps.title: It is about finding vessels, like our משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that רב ששת's list is about finding vessels with images, matching our משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is obviously about someone who finds such vessels, as we learned in the משנה: One who finds vessels with a figure of the sun, the moon or a dragon on them must take them to the Dead Sea.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the correct answer: רב ששת is talking about someone who finds vessels with images on them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Making images is forbidden by the פסוק, so "permitted" must mean a found vessel may be kept and used. This matches our משנה, where only vessels with the sun, moon or dragon must be destroyed.

keyTerms.meaning: as we learned in a משנה

steps.whatToRemember: Making images of the heavenly bodies is forbidden by the Torah, so the first line of רב ששת's list cannot be about making images. For now the גמרא reads it as being about finding vessels, but the next step challenges this reading.
steps.whyThisMatters: It keeps two separate laws apart: the ban on making images, and the rule about benefiting from found vessels with images.

phrases.english: Rather, it is obviously about one who finds them,
and it is as we learned:
One who finds vessels, and on them is

phrases.aramaic: צוּרַת חַמָּה, צוּרַת לְבָנָה, צוּרַת דְּרָקוֹן —
phrases.english: a figure of the sun, a figure of the moon, or a figure of a dragon,
phrases.notes: This is our משנה from step 12.

phrases.english: must take them to the Dead Sea.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the correct answer after step 18 rejected the first option.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב ששת's list is about finding vessels with images, just like the case in our משנה.

steps.title: If it's about finding, why is the human face forbidden?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that רב ששת's list is about finding vessels. Our משנה lists only sun, moon and dragon as forbidden finds, not a human face.
steps.simpleTranslation: If רב ששת is talking about finding vessels, look at the middle part of his list: all faces are permitted except a human face. But when you find vessels, is a human face forbidden? Our משנה says that if you find vessels with a sun, moon or dragon on them, you throw them into ים המלח. A dragon is listed, but a human face is not!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the reading from step 19 against the middle line of רב ששת's list and finds a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת forbids a human face. But the משנה, which is about finding vessels, never mentions a human face. So if רב ששת were talking about finding, he would be adding a prohibition that the משנה does not have.

keyTerms.meaning: The Dead Sea, where forbidden items are thrown so no one benefits from them

phrases.english: If it is about one who finds,
say the middle clause:
all faces are permitted
except for the human face;
if it is about one who finds,
is a human face forbidden?
But didn't we learn in the משנה:
one who finds vessels, and upon them is
a figure of the sun, a figure of the moon,
a figure of a dragon:
he must take them to the Dead Sea.
A figure of a dragon, yes,
a human face, no!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the conclusion of step 19 that רב ששת's list is about finding.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that רב ששת's list refers to finding vessels.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה about finding lists sun, moon and dragon but not a human face, so a list about finding cannot forbid a human face.

steps.title: Rather, the list is about making images
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא switches: the list must be about making images, and forming a human face is forbidden according to רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is obvious that he is talking about someone who makes an image, and this follows the teaching of רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the finding reading failed, the גמרא now says רב ששת's list is about making images.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Making a human face is forbidden because of רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע's teaching. That explains why רב ששת lists the human face. This reverses the reading from steps 18-19, which had pushed away the making reading.

keyTerms.meaning: One who makes or forms (an image)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't get dizzy: in step 18 the גמרא rejected 'making' because making images of the other constellations is forbidden too. Now it goes back to 'making' because of the human face. The גמרא is checking each clause of the list against both readings.

phrases.english: Rather, it is obvious that it is about one who makes,
and in line with רב הונא son of רב יהושע.
phrases.notes: His teaching comes later in the מסכת: "don't make with Me" means don't form a human face, since a person is made in God's image.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 20 by switching the list from finding to making.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב ששת's list is about finding vessels.
steps.terutzMaskana: At least the human-face clause is about making an image, which is forbidden according to רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע.

steps.title: If it's about making, why is a dragon forbidden?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the making reading from the last clause of the list. Why would forming a dragon be forbidden? It quotes ״לא תעשון אתי״ to frame the challenge.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he is talking about making images, look at the end of his list: all figures are permitted except a dragon. But is making a dragon forbidden? Isn't it written, ״You shall not make with Me gods of silver and gods of gold״?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the new making reading against the last line of רב ששת's list and raises a challenge from a פסוק. The challenge continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the dragon is the problem. The prohibition on making images comes from the פסוק ״לא תעשון אתי״, and the גמרא suggests a dragon does not fall under it. So under the making reading, the dragon clause seems out of place.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it written (a challenge from a פסוק)
"You shall not make with Me", the source for forbidden image-making

phrases.english: If it is about one who makes,
say the last clause:
all figures are permitted
except for the figure of a dragon;
and if it is about one who makes,
is the figure of a dragon forbidden?
But isn't it written:
"You shall not make with Me
gods of silver and gods of gold",
phrases.notes: שמות 20:20. The גמרא keeps explaining this פסוק on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the making reading that step 21 just proposed, using the last clause of רב ששת's list.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that רב ששת's list refers to making images.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rules for making images come from ״לא תעשון אתי״, and the dragon does not seem to fall under that פסוק, so a list about making should not forbid a dragon.
